findings.title: Future or stale evidence can bypass SENSE admission
findings.detail: evaluate_think trusts SenseResult.usable without validating its temporal bounds, while SenseResult has no constructor invariants. A caller can directly construct a SenseResult containing future or stale usable evidence and no rejected entries; THINK then returns admitted beliefs influenced by that evidence. This violates the fail-closed point-in-time requirement.

findings.title: Malformed invalidation identifiers are admitted
findings.detail: InvalidationCondition checks only truthiness, so non-string condition IDs and claim keys are accepted and evaluate_think can return an admitted result containing them. This violates the typed-contract and fail-closed malformed-input requirements.

findings.title: Calibration rule is mutable external state
findings.detail: evaluate_think derives confidence weights and its calibration label from module-level bindings reachable through atp.brain.think. MappingProxyType blocks item mutation, but callers can replace _QUALITY_WEIGHT or CALIBRATION_VERSION, changing scores, calibration labels, and checksums for identical explicit inputs. This violates the immutable-calibration and mutable-module-state invariants.

findings.title: Timestamp validation can admit absolute-future evidence
findings.detail: Aware datetimes are compared without first normalizing them to UTC. During a DST fold, wall-time comparison can admit evidence that is later in absolute time and can produce different admission results for equivalent UTC representations, violating point-in-time safety and timezone equivalence.
